facts.text: Current docs emphasize tab-local search/filtering in Run Graph, Evidence, and Ledger; History is list/table oriented.
Cross-surface navigation exists in fragments (Graph->Evidence/Usage, History->Graph/Evidence, Ledger->Usage).
Storage model already has canonical seglog, Tantivy as intended full-text layer, and project-scoped indices.
No unified Orchestrator search contract currently exists that is object-first rather than page-first.
Final GUI spec already defines a global command palette.
Historical semantics are explicit for attempts/block projections, but uneven for higher-level objects.

decisions.text: Distinguish global Orchestrator object search from tab-local filtering.
Make Orchestrator search object-first, run-aware, and route-aware.
Search result rows should carry canonical routing payload: focused_run_id, destination tab, selected object id, optional filter payload, optional detail target.
Command palette object results should reuse the same deep-link routing contract as Orchestrator search.
Backend search should prioritize stable identity matches before full-text hits.
Semantic state model should separate time status, replacement status, and validity status.

constraints.text: Search routing must preserve or intentionally change focused_run_id and never change run focus silently.
Search should identify objects even when user does not know owning tab first.
Historical lineage must remain visible even when live targets disappear.

risks.text: Without a shared routing payload, search/deeplinks/cross-tab navigation can diverge into incompatible systems.
Undefined run-scope behavior risks confusing result sets and accidental context shifts.
Relying on full-text alone without object-side contract may produce weak relevance and unstable targeting.
Collapsing historical states into a generic old state loses important operational semantics.

open_questions.text: Which destination (Ledger vs History) should be canonical for promotion/review/corroboration/graph-patch/recovery records by default?
What exact object/record contract should combine redb projections with Tantivy for unified search ranking and retrieval?

actions.text: Define a canonical Orchestrator search result contract including identity, type, run implications, destination tab, and selection/filter payload.
Implement explicit UX disclosure when focused run changes due to search result selection.
Unify routing contract across search results, command palette results, deep links, and Show in actions.
Adopt shared semantic vocabulary for historical/current status dimensions across promotions, concerns, graph patches, recovery records, and lane/worktree lifecycle.

requirements.text: Object-first search targets should include at minimum:
Search results should not merely highlight text.
Each result should carry a canonical route target:
when a result belongs to another run, selecting it should explicitly switch the focused run
the UI should disclose that the focused run changed because of the search result
search result routing must preserve or intentionally change `focused_run_id`
it must never do so silently
selecting an object result should route through the same deep-link contract as Orchestrator search
search should prefer stable object identity matches first
Search should help the user find the right object, not force them to know which tab owns it first.
Historical results must preserve run context clearly so search does not create silent run-focus jumps.
historical lineage must remain visible even when live targets disappear
These should not collapse into a generic "old" state.
